documents.title: AI & Academic Integrity - Artificial Intelligence & Information Literacy
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Using AI without permission or proper citation' can lead to violations and tells students to 'Ask instructors about their AI use policies', so it sets no default allowance or ban itself and leaves permission to instructors; this is delegates.
documents.summary: A short library guide page that says unpermitted or uncited AI use can count as plagiarism or a conduct violation. It gives students four tips: ask instructors about their AI policies, treat AI as a source not a substitute, cite AI in the class's citation style, and treat AI tools as aids rather than authors. It sets no rule of its own and is not an official provost or integrity-office policy.

units.why: The guide opens with 'VSU upholds academic honesty', giving academic honesty as the ground for the AI rules that follow; it is a principle (informs, general), so P95 (fairness/honesty rationale) fits better than P41 skill-building.

The sentence says 'Using AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations', classing unpermitted or uncited AI use as misconduct; P36 fits, and no penalties are named so not P37. Addressed to students.
units.anchor: AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations.

units.why: The tip 'Ask instructors about their AI use policies' tells students to check with the instructor before using AI; this is P10 (ask), and it also implies the instructor sets the rule, but the directive to students is the main content.
units.anchor: Ask instructors about their AI use policies

units.why: The tip 'Treat AI like a source, not a substitute' says AI should inform student work but not replace it; this is closest to P32 (student stays primary problem-solver), though P96 and P45 do not fit since it calls AI a source.
units.fit_note: The tip also casts AI as a 'source' (to be cited), which P32 does not capture.

units.why: The tip 'Cite AI tools using your class’s citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)' directs students to cite AI use in their work, giving no detail of prompt or output, so P24 rather than P25.
units.anchor: Cite AI tools using your class’s citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)

units.why: The reminder 'tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors' says AI is not the author of submitted work, which matches P96 (AI as neither author nor collaborator).
units.anchor: tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors.

notes: Single thin library guide; no official VSU-wide policy found. The guide is not an integrity-office policy.
